bull_bear.body:
- Single largest manufacturer of country liquor in Maharashtra, contributing about 25-30% of the state's total excise duty collected on country liquor
- Consistently good brand image and loyalty from consumers built over several years, giving substantial market share in Mumbai, Thane & Palghar
- Pioneered product-format innovation in the category: introduced 180 ml bottles to the country liquor industry (previously only 750 & 375 ml were made) and popularised PET bottles, which now account for ~92.72% of production and ~92.74% of sales
- Bottling lines designed to handle both glass and PET bottles, insulating operations from the outcome of the pending PET-bottle litigation
- Surplus manufacturing capacity (utilisation only 59.59% last year) provides headroom to expand into interior Maharashtra districts without fresh capex
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Illicit / duty-evaded liquor market — Management flags the parallel duty-evaded market as the major threat to the company, eroding both its market share and government excise revenue; the company continues to make representations to Government to curb it.
- High and frequently-changing taxation — Very high levels of taxation and frequent changes in laws create difficulty for the company; management states the exorbitant tax rate is itself one of the factors that breeds duty evasion in the market.
- Raw material (Rectified Spirit) price volatility and shortage — High fluctuations in the price of Rectified Spirit, the main raw material, combined with acute shortages in its availability, have been a persistent constraint over several years.
- PET bottle packaging cost volatility — PET bottles account for ~92.72% of production, so the company is exposed to sudden spurts in PET bottle prices driven by international petroleum prices and forex fluctuations, as experienced last year.
- Conflicting multi-agency regulatory jurisdiction — The company faces concurrent and parallel jurisdiction of multiple government agencies (State Excise Department, Legal Metrology Department, FDA) whose requirements management describes as conflicting in nature.
- Pending litigation on PET bottle usage notification — A Maharashtra government notification banning PET bottles for alcoholic liquor (effective April 1, 2016) is under challenge via writ petitions in the Bombay High Court, which has granted an interim stay still in force with no final judgment; management states the eventual outcome will not affect operations since all bottling lines can handle both glass and PET.
- Unquantifiable near-term impact from combined deterrents — Management states that the illicit market, taxation, and input-cost/regulatory factors together are expected to have a serious impact on the business in the current financial year, but that the impact cannot be quantified or its timing forecast.
